notes.summary: Internet, email and networking give 4–5 Tier 2 questions: full forms, protocols and ports, network types (PAN/LAN/MAN/WAN), topologies, network devices and IP addressing.

concepts.title: Internet basics
concepts.body:
• WWW was invented by Tim Berners-Lee (1989). ARPANET (1969) was the first network.
  • URL = Uniform Resource Locator, e.g. https://www.example.com/page.
  • DNS converts a domain name into an IP address.
  • HTTP transfers web pages (port 80); HTTPS is the secure version (port 443). FTP transfers files.
  • HTML is the language for building web pages; a browser (Chrome, Firefox) displays them.

concepts.title: Email
concepts.body:
• SMTP sends email; POP3 and IMAP receive email (IMAP keeps mail on the server).
  • CC = Carbon Copy (everyone sees); BCC = Blind Carbon Copy (hidden from other receivers).
  • Email address format: username@domain. Unwanted bulk mail is spam.

concepts.title: Networks, topologies and devices
concepts.body:
• By area: PAN (a person, Bluetooth) < LAN (a building) < MAN (a city) < WAN (country / world; the Internet is the largest WAN).
  • Topologies: Star (all to a central hub/switch), Bus (one backbone cable), Ring (closed loop), Mesh (every node to every node), Tree (hierarchy of stars).
  • Devices: Hub (broadcasts to all), Switch (sends to the right MAC address), Router (joins different networks using IP), Modem (digital ↔ analog), Gateway (joins networks using different protocols), Repeater (boosts signal).
  • IPv4 = 32 bits; IPv6 = 128 bits; MAC address = 48 bits.

varieties.name: Internet terms and protocols
varieties.how: Learn full forms and what each protocol does, with its common port.

example.q: Which system translates www.example.com into an IP address?
steps: Names are for people; computers need IP addresses.
The Domain Name System does this lookup.

varieties.name: Email protocols and fields
varieties.how: SMTP sends, POP3/IMAP receive; CC visible, BCC hidden.

example.q: Which protocol keeps emails on the server and syncs them across devices?
steps: POP3 usually downloads and removes mail from the server.
IMAP keeps mail on the server and syncs folders.

varieties.name: Network types, topologies and devices
varieties.how: Use the area (PAN/LAN/MAN/WAN), the shape (star/bus/ring/mesh) and the job of the device.

example.q: How many links are needed for a full mesh of 5 computers?
steps: Each pair needs one link: n(n − 1)/2

tips: Port numbers: HTTP 80, HTTPS 443, FTP 21, SMTP 25, POP3 110, IMAP 143, SSH 22, DNS 53.
In a star topology, if the hub fails the whole network fails; if one cable fails only that node is lost.
A full mesh of n nodes needs n(n − 1)/2 links.
traps: A modem is not a router: the modem converts signals, the router chooses paths between networks.
BCC receivers are hidden from others; CC receivers are visible.
The Internet and the World Wide Web are not the same: WWW is a service that runs on the Internet.

questions.q: Who invented the World Wide Web?
questions.solution: Tim Berners-Lee created the WWW in 1989 at CERN. Vint Cerf co-designed TCP/IP and Ray Tomlinson sent the first email.
BCC = Blind Carbon Copy. Addresses in BCC are not shown to the other receivers.

questions.q: A network that covers an entire city is called a:
questions.solution: MAN = Metropolitan Area Network, covering a city. LAN covers a building, PAN a single person, WAN a country or the world.

questions.q: In which topology are all computers connected to a single central hub or switch?
questions.solution: In a star topology every node has its own cable to a central hub/switch.

questions.q: Which protocol is used to transfer web pages securely, using encryption?
questions.solution: HTTPS (HTTP Secure) encrypts web traffic using TLS/SSL and uses port 443. Plain HTTP (port 80) is not encrypted.

questions.q: Which device connects two different networks and forwards data packets using IP addresses?
questions.solution: A router joins different networks and picks the path for each packet using IP addresses. A hub just broadcasts, a repeater boosts signal, a modem converts digital/analog.

questions.q: How many bits are used in an IPv6 address?
questions.solution: IPv6 uses 128-bit addresses. IPv4 uses 32 bits and a MAC address has 48 bits.

questions.q: Which protocol is used to SEND email from a client to a mail server?
questions.solution: SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) sends mail. POP3 and IMAP are used to receive/read it; SNMP is for network management.

flashcards.back: Domain Name System: converts domain names to IP addresses
SMTP sends email; POP3 and IMAP receive it
Hub broadcasts to all ports; switch sends only to the target device (MAC address)
